_comment: Central question bank for the 2026 hackathon. Each entry: id (stable), difficulty (easy|medium|hard), title, and text (array of lines, joined with newlines at load). Referenced by id from the per-student assignments table and embedded as a header in downloaded submission files. Edit here + redeploy to change questions.

questions.title: Find the Day of the Week (Zeller's Congruence)
text: During a cybersecurity audit, a team of digital forensics experts recovered an encrypted archive containing thousands of historical records. Every record is indexed by the exact day of the week it was created, but the original calendar software is no longer available. Fortunately, the engineers discovered that the system relied on Zeller's Congruence, a mathematical algorithm that determines the day of the week for any given date. Your task is to recreate this functionality without using any built-in date or calendar libraries.
1. Take the last two digits of the year.
2. Add the last two digits of the year divided by 4 (ignore the remainder).
3. Add the day of the month.
6. If it is a leap year and the month is January or February, subtract 1.
7. Divide the total by 7 and take the remainder.
Develop a program that asks the user to enter a day, month, and year, then determines the correct day of the week using Zeller's Congruence.
Display the result in the following format:

Develop a program that allows the user to play a Best of Three game of Rock, Paper, Scissors against the computer. The computer's choice must be selected randomly each round.
